title: Lease-handoff preemptor for cooperative KV eviction and GPU compaction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a cooperative 'lease-handoff' preemption strategy that reduces hard interrupts while preserving SLOs by coordinating KV cache eviction, progressive GPU slab compaction, and short-lived request leases. This ticket scopes the algorithm, runtime integration, telemetry, and a small canary rollout on dedicated pools. Goal: reduce 95th and 99th p99 tail latency regressions under high KV pressure while improving overall fairness across tenants without dramatic increases in token cost.
decision_notes: After spike and microbenchmarks, we favor a cooperative lease-handoff approach over immediate hard preemption. Trade-offs: more complexity and a short increase in path length (lease negotiation), but substantially fewer disruptive KV evictions and smoother latency tails. We'll combine predictive per-request KV lifetime scoring (lightweight ML heuristic from telemetry) with a bounded lease duration and a two-stage GPU compaction pass to reclaim memory non-disruptively.
technical_notes: Key components: (1) Lease manager attached to batching ingress that issues 50-200ms soft leases under high pressure. (2) KV lifetime estimator using recent token reuse histograms per-model-per-tenant (low-cost, on-device sliding window). (3) Cooperative handoff protocol: when preemption is needed, we solicit voluntary batch yield from low-priority leases and migrate their KV handles to a transient reservation slab rather than immediate eviction. (4) Progressive compaction: background GPU kernel that compacts short-lived slabs first, with eviction only if compaction fails to free enough memory.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canary on two dedicated pools shows no more than 5% increase in median latency and 0-2% decrease in throughput while 95th and 99th latency improve vs current hard-preempt baseline under a synthetic KV-heavy workload.
2) Platform emits new metrics: lease_granted, lease_relinquished, kv_handoff_count, compaction_cycles, preemptions_skipped.
3) No regression in cost per token >3% on average for affected tenants during canary.
4) Playbook and rollback documented; canary can be disabled via runtime flag in <10m.
